bibliography.abstract: Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer (DWPT) could eliminate plug-in charging in cities, but optimal urban deployment is complex. This paper develops a mixed-integer programming model that optimizes DWPT location under signalized intersection dynamics -- acceleration, deceleration, and queue-position-dependent dwell time -- through probabilistic signal patterns and saturation headway-based modeling. A case study of Kawagoe City, Japan, shows that electrifying 1.5% of the road network is sufficient to sustain continuous urban EV operation without plug-in charging for the baseline scenario, and at most 2.9% suffices across all tested assumptions. Monte Carlo simulations of continuous trip chains averaging approximately 600 km and reaching up to approximately 800 km confirm that optimized 12 kWh-battery deployments sustain operation in all simulated runs, revealing an infrastructure-battery tradeoff corresponding to roughly 1.7-3.0 tonnes CO2e of avoided battery manufacturing emissions per vehicle relative to a conventional 40 kWh urban EV. These findings position DWPT deployment as an environmentally efficient pathway for sustainable urban mobility when deployed optimally.
bibliography.title: Infinite Drive: Optimal Urban Location of Dynamic Wireless Charging at Signalized Intersections

en.caveats: The findings are based on a simulation model applied to a single Japanese city and rely on probabilistic signal patterns and saturation headway assumptions that may vary in other urban contexts.
en.what: The study develops a mixed-integer programming model to optimize the placement of Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer (DWPT) infrastructure at signalized intersections, accounting for vehicle acceleration, deceleration, and queue-dependent dwell times. Applying this model to Kawagoe City, Japan, and running Monte Carlo simulations of continuous trip chains up to 800 km, the researchers found that electrifying just 1.5% to 2.9% of the road network is sufficient to keep electric vehicles with 12 kWh batteries running continuously without plug-in charging.
en.why: It demonstrates that strategic, intersection-focused wireless charging can eliminate the need for large vehicle batteries, avoiding an estimated 1.7 to 3.0 tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions from battery manufacturing per vehicle compared to a standard 40 kWh urban electric vehicle.
